newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Importer dollar demand saw the South African rand motor up in late trade, breaking through the 4.50 level on the dollar but dealers said the move was temporary and did not signal a new trend.
At 1412 GMT the rand was at 4.5020/5070 on the dollar from 4.4905/4955 in late trade on Thursday after edging weaker throughout the day.

"The market was caught short of dollars at the 4.4910/4950 level and drifted up from there but we are still expecting a range of around 4.4850/5120 in the short-term...nothing much has changed," a senior trader noted.

The rand's upward move was triggered late on Thursday by the release of the Reserve Bank's quarterly bulletin. The market reacted negatively to figures confirming that South Africa recorded a current account deficit of 4.619 billion rand in the three months to June 30.
But dealers said it had been a "knee-jerk" reaction.

"The market is looking for any excuse at the moment to break out of its tight range and even though the figure was nothing new, we saw importer dollar demand and the market was caught short," the trader said.
Another trader said a U.S. investment house started buying dollars late on Thursday and demand followed through early on Friday although there had also been good exporter interest.
The Reserve Bank was expected to step into the market early next week if the currency broke decisively above 4.50 on the dollar, halting any further upward moves, traders said.
Against the crosses, the currency weakened to 7.0009/0088 against sterling from 6.9533/9655 overnight but was steady at 0.3361/3365 marks from 0.3369/3375 marks previously.
Long bonds yields also pushed higher and the market ended the day on a slightly weaker note after drifting sideways in a range of around 14.91 to 14.99 pct during the week.
At 1412 GMT the key R150 stock was at 15.04 percent from 14.99 percent overnight.
"Trade was lacklustre and it's difficult to call direction...everyone talked the market stronger this week but it did not happen," a trader at one of the big four local banks said.
Dealers said the market was looking towards U.S. rates ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve open market committee meeting next Tuesday for direction.

"That is the next major event," the dealer said but noted that the market would only react on Wednesday if the Fed hiked interest rates as financial markets in South Africa would be closed on Tuesday for a public holiday.
Another trader agreed that sentiment had turned mixed after a bullish phase.
"The money market shortage is back above the eight billion mark, the rand is hovering around 4.50...I would say that a bit of bearishness is creeping into the market," he said.
Bond Exchange figures showed foreigners were net sellers of 2.57 million rand of South African bonds on Thursday after buying 60.32 million rand worth on Wednesday.
On the money market, three-month NCDs were steady at between 15.70 to 15.90 percent while 90-day BAs edged lower to between 15.15 to 15.30 percent from between 15.15 to 15.35 percent.
The Reserve Bank said the daily shortage rose to over eight billion rand to be quoted at 8.018 billion rand from 7.589 billion rand on Wednesday.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
